query: If films addressed the most common audience complaints, how much would positive sentiment increase?

per_column.name: primary_complaint_category
per_column.rationale: The query centers on 'the most common audience complaints'; this column identifies the complaint category that would be addressed. Addressing/fixing a complaint category is an intervenable lever a filmmaker could act on, so it functions as the treatment. It is explicitly implied by the query.

per_column.name: complaint_intensity_level
per_column.rationale: Intensity of the complaint is a graded characterization of the complaint itself, lying on the path between having a complaint and the resulting sentiment. It is a consequence/aspect of the treatment rather than a common cause of both treatment and outcome, so it is not a confounder.

per_column.name: plot_quality_deficit
per_column.rationale: This is a finer-grained decomposition of a specific complaint (plot). It is another aspect of the same complaint construct being intervened on, an intervenable deficit that could be fixed, not a common cause of both treatment and outcome. It does not act as a confounder.

judge.rationale: The added columns capture the treatment side of the what-if question—identifying and decomposing the audience complaints that films could 'address'—and these are genuinely intervenable levers (a filmmaker can fix plot, pacing, acting, etc.). However, the intervention framing is incomplete: NO confounders were added. To read off a counterfactual effect of addressing complaints on positive sentiment, one must adjust for common causes of BOTH which complaints arise AND baseline sentiment (e.g., genre, budget/production tier, reviewer expectations, star power, franchise/expectation effects, viewer demographics). None of these were introduced, and complaint_intensity_level is a mediator/aspect of the treatment rather than a confounder. The set therefore establishes the treatment but fails the decisive test: it supplies zero confounders (named or unnamed), so the counterfactual effect is not identifiable.
